summary: Wuhan Tianhe International Airport is the principal aviation gateway for Wuhan, the capital of Hubei Province in central China. Opened in 1995 and located in the Huangpi District roughly 26 km north of the city center, it serves as a major hub for China Southern Airlines and operates two passenger terminals handling domestic and international flights. The airport sits near the confluence of the Yangtze and Han rivers, one of China's most significant inland economic corridors.
faqs:
Q: How far is Wuhan Tianhe International Airport from the city center?
A: The airport is approximately 26 km (16 miles) north of Wuhan's city center in Huangpi District, typically a 40-60 minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: Does the airport have a metro connection?
A: Yes, Wuhan Metro Line 2 connects the airport directly to central Wuhan, with Terminal 2 station providing convenient access to Hankou and Wuchang districts.

Q: Which airlines use Wuhan Tianhe as a hub?
A: China Southern Airlines operates its main hub here, with additional significant service from China Eastern, Hainan Airlines, and numerous international carriers.

Q: Are there sleeping facilities or transit hotels at the airport?
A: The airport offers rest areas, VIP lounges, and nearby hotels; some terminal lounges provide napping zones for transit passengers, though dedicated transit hotels are limited.
transport_tips: The metro Line 2 is the most reliable and cost-effective option to reach central Wuhan, with trains running approximately every 6-8 minutes. Airport express buses serve various city districts and neighboring cities, while official taxi queues at arrivals use metered fares; ride-hailing apps like Didi also operate but pickup zones are designated outside terminals. Allow extra time during rush hours, as the airport expressway can experience significant congestion.
local_tip: Frequent travelers recommend buying a Wuhan Tong (transport card) before your trip if you plan to use public transit extensively—it works on the metro, buses, and ferries, and saves time versus buying single tickets, especially useful if you want to explore the Yellow Crane Tower or East Lake during a layover or extended visit.
